- Latency SLO: <200ms 95th for single-request flows, occasional batch summarization acceptable up to 1s.

Two asks (to finalize cost sketch)
1) Expected steady-state monthly token volume (best guess or range) — you had mentioned a pilot, then roll to 3 regions. Please give a low/expected/high.
2) Peak TPS / concurrency windows — what does your traffic look like at peak? burst length?

If easier, a single-line answer like: low=10M/mo, expected=75M/mo, high=300M/mo; peak=120 TPS sustained for ~10m, burst to 350 TPS for 60s — that will let us give unit-econ and SLA options.

I attached a lightweight token estimate template you can drop numbers into. Once we have ranges, I’ll put together three pricing scenarios (self-serve hosted, committed monthly slab, and dedicated-reserved) and indicate likely $/1M token targets.

Next steps: Emily — can you confirm numbers by Monday 4/14? I’ll follow up internally with the pricing baseline.

—Kimberly

Short note with pricing suggestions based on Emily's ranges and our hosted unit economics: 

Assumptions used:
- Avg token composition per call = 1k tokens (as Emily noted).
- Baseline HW & ops cost per token at this scale -> our internal blended cost => ~$6.50 / 1M tokens (current hosted mix with prefix caching).

Proposed bands (hosted API) — list price / committed discount / gross margin note:
1) Pay-as-you-go (no commitment)
   - List: $30 / 1M tokens
   - Expect low margin; for small pilots it's fine
2) 1-month committed slab (recommended for Q3 pilot->rollout)
   - List: $20 / 1M tokens
   - Proposed promotional: $17 / 1M for first 3 months (if they commit to >=40M/mo)
   - Margin: healthy at expected volumes
3) 3-month committed slab (better economics for us + Peregrine predictability)
   - List: $16 / 1M tokens
   - Promotional: $14 / 1M with 3-month minimum commit (>=45M/mo)

Burst handling (operational note):
- Sustained 160 TPS for 5m is fine on hosted; short bursts to 420 TPS for <90s are also supportable via short-term autoscale + burst buffer but we should price for it if they expect frequent occurrences. Recommend we include a one-time ramp window allowance and then charge for sustained burst usage beyond X occurrences. Ops (Karthik) to confirm exact guardrails.

Next step: Kimberly — if you’re good with these bands I can draft a 1-pager with the three scenarios and the estimated monthly bill for low/expected/high. Also include sample SLA banding: 95th p95 <200ms for paid slab, 99th SLO for enterprise/dedicated.

-Marissa

Emily — thanks for the fast turnaround and for populating the sheet. We ran a quick pricing sketch and attached a short scenario summary (inline below):

Inline summary (expected case ~45M/mo)
- Pay-as-you-go: ~$1,350 / month (45 * $30 / 1M) — useful for pilot but variable.
- 1-month slab (promo): ~$765 (45 * $17 / 1M) — recommended to minimize unit cost during rollout.
- 3-month slab (promo): ~$630 (45 * $14 / 1M) — best unit econ, requires short commit.

Burst & SLA note: we can handle the described bursts on hosted with a short burst buffer; if Peregrine will have repeated daily bursts to ~420 TPS we'll want to discuss a short-term burst package (flat fee for N bursts per month) or move to Dedicated for guaranteed concurrency.
